phase: 1 - grooming and training end-to-end, driven in a real browser with demo data
status: FIXED - Option 2 (site root books through the governed grooming flow)
title: The public landing page's grooming flow is not the governed customer journey, and cannot complete a booking on any real host
method: Drove app/page.tsx (the site root) in Chromium as a brand-new ANONYMOUS context - no session cookie at all - and again with the signed-in demo customer's session.
measured: The header reads 'Login' even when a valid customer session cookie is present: the page never reads the session. `grep -c` for every customer-session import in app/page.tsx returns 0.

Pressing 'Confirm booking' opens a modal, 'Confirm your mobile number', carrying the line 'Prototype note: OTP verification is simulated for review.' Pressing Continue issued ZERO network requests - the note is literally true, nothing is verified.
The 'Select 1 registered pet' list is a hardcoded module-level fixture, app/page.tsx:29-36 (bruno, milo, max, rio, coco, luna, simba) - not the customer's pets.
On confirm, the requests carried customerId:'WEB-9812345678' - an identity synthesised from the unverified phone - and petIds:['bruno'].

With a groomer roster published locally, the flow completed: booking PS-UAT-MTB2FAUM-F62A confirmed, work order WO-C308F819 to a real groomer, payment PAY-AAFE546C, and a NEW canonical pet PET-WEB981234567-31E645A314E2AD54150C minted from the fixture.

refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.what_I_first_suspected: That an anonymous visitor can create confirmed canonical bookings with no identity verification.
refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.why_that_is_wrong: The local run reached those endpoints only because localhost + NODE_ENV=development activates the development-preview actor (lib/development-preview.ts).
refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.measured_refutation: Driving the same real POST handlers with a non-preview request host returns 401 {"error":"Authentication required"} for BOTH /api/uat-scheduling and /api/canonical-bookings. The authorization control holds. This is stated plainly because the earlier reading was mine and it was wrong.

what_is_actually_wrong: The flow books a FIXTURE pet, not the customer's own. app/mobile-app/training-flow.tsx was already corrected for exactly this - tests/training-customer-wiring.test.mjs pins 'books the signed-in customer's own dogs, never a fixture identity'. The grooming landing page was never brought along.
Identity is derived as WEB-<phone> from a number the flow does not verify, so it is not the authenticated customer identity the rest of the platform uses.

Because it holds no session, on any host that is not a development preview its FIRST API call returns 401 - after the customer has entered name, phone, secondary phone, doorstep address, pet, safety notes and payment preference. A real customer on the live site cannot complete a grooming booking here and only finds out at the end.

app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx is the governed twin: it loads the customer's own pets, resolves the service location, and books through createCanonicalLifecycle. app/mobile-app/page.tsx renders it EMBEDDED. So a correct grooming journey exists; the site root runs a different, older one.
severity: Launch-blocking for the grooming journey as presented on the public site, and only for that surface. No data was exposed and no control was bypassed.
not_claimed: No production or staging system was touched. Every measurement is local.
The booking created during this probe exists only in the local .wrangler dev database.

remedy_chosen_by_the_product_owner.option: Option 2 - the public entry hands booking to app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx, gated behind real sign-in
remedy_chosen_by_the_product_owner.why_this_is_not_the_audit_inventing_sema: The choice between routing / to the governed flow, gating its own CTA, or making / marketing-only was put to the product owner and Option 2 was returned. This ledger records the instruction, it does not originate it.

what_changed: app/page.tsx no longer runs its own booking. It loads the authenticated customer with loadCustomerAccount(); 'Confirm booking' renders <GroomingFlow customer={...}/> when signed in and <CustomerLogin/> (the real OTP screen) when signed out.

Deleted from app/page.tsx: the savedPets module fixture, verifyOtp, finishBooking, both modals including the 'OTP verification is simulated for review' note, the confirmed-booking branch, and the state and handlers that only served them. Net -287 lines, +39.

app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx was corrected where it was WEAKER than the entry page it replaces, so no behaviour was lost in the move: the safety-notes / bite-history question was carried over into pricing requirements; bookingNonce() (a per-call random value, so a resubmit created a second booking) was replaced with stableBookingInputKey() over the 17 booking inputs, restoring deduplication; a re-entrancy guard was added to the scheduling submit.
lib/booking-input-fingerprint.ts is new: FNV-1a over the inputs joined by U+001F. Deterministic - no clock, no randomness - which is what makes the resubmit collapse onto the same booking.

fifth_behaviour_loss_found_during_implem.defect: app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx declared status: pay==="online" ? "captured" : "created" - the client asserting money was received, with no gateway attestation. This is the same defect class as PTJA-P1-F32 (Training), which was fixed in an earlier closure.
fifth_behaviour_loss_found_during_implem.correction: status is now always "created"; initialPaymentStatus carries pay==="online" ? "payment_pending" : "due_after_service". Verified that grooming governance, unlike boarding/sitting/training, does not require captured, so this does not block the journey.
fifth_behaviour_loss_found_during_implem.measured: booking_payments.status = 'created' with detail 'Pay now, sandbox authorization pending; live capture not connected'.
fifth_behaviour_loss_found_during_implem.shadowed_test: tests/rendered-html.test.mjs asserted the fabricated capture as a contract. It was retargeted to assert the corrected behaviour, not relaxed.

verification.focused: tests/ptja-p1-04-governed-grooming-entry.test.mjs - 12 cases, unique namespace, no shared globals
verification.browser_signed_out: real OTP login shown ('Enter your phone number to sign in or create your account'); no simulated-OTP note; no WEB- or TST-101 identity in any request
verification.browser_signed_in: governed flow reached; the customer's real pet 'Bruno Labrador Retriever' listed; fixture pets Milo/Coco/Rio absent; safety question present with all three options
verification.dedup: FIRST 201 PS-UAT-MTBAZ6LM-64F6 duplicatePrevented=false; RESUBMIT same inputs 200 same id duplicatePrevented=true; DB row count for that key = 1
verification.provider_proof_endpoint: groom_arun -> verified:false, stats:null, isNewProvider:true; unknown provider -> 404

remaining_uncertainty: Provider-proof ON-SCREEN visibility was not obtained in the browser: the flow's 'Verify service address' step could not be driven from Playwright (the Check button stayed disabled under both fill() and pressSequentially()). The proof block itself is covered by the gate test, the negative-case test, sabotage, and the live endpoint behaviour above - but it was not seen rendered.
why_it_was_not_fixed_at_audit_time: The remedy is a product decision, not a defect fix: route / to the governed flow, gate its CTA behind real sign-in, or make / marketing-only and send booking to /mobile-app. Each changes what the public site does. Choosing one would be inventing product semantics, which this audit does not do.
